description: Korean glossary of the game's own text (docs/modding/translation-handbook.md). terms: English term of glossary_en.json -> the Korean form used in every file. keep_latin: Latin words the validator accepts in the Korean text. style: the rules of voice and form.

style.address: Speech levels. Harry and Cybil: polite haeyo-che both ways, 'X 씨'. Harry and Lisa: haeyo-che both ways; Lisa says '해리 씨', Harry says '리사'. Harry and Kaufmann: formal hapsyo/haeyo both ways in the hospital and the bar; in the motel Kaufmann drops to banmal in anger, Harry stays polite. Dahlia to Harry and Cybil: archaic hao-che with '그대'; Dahlia to Alessa: motherly haera-che ('~하렴', '~란다'); Dahlia to Kaufmann and in her monologues: solemn haera-che. Harry to Dahlia: polite until the last scene, banmal in the last scene. Kaufmann to Dahlia: banmal. Cheryl and Alessa to a parent: a child's banmal ('아빠', '엄마'). Harry to the girl at the amusement park (Alessa): banmal. Harry to the aliens: formal hapsyo-che. Harry's own thoughts and all narration: plain form ('~다', '~군', '~인가?').
style.quotes: “ ” for the [ ] of the English (speech, titles, inscriptions); the dash of broken speech is the character — (U+2014), one per '=' of the English; the ellipsis is three full stops as in the English.
style.item_in_sentence: one pattern, the particle chosen by the final consonant of the item name: '<name>이/가 있다. 가져갈까?', '<name>을/를 사용했다.', '<name>을/를 손에 넣었다.'
style.line_breaks: lines break between eojeol only; a Hangul syllable is 12 px, a space 6 px, about 20 syllables to a 300 px line.
style.notes: notes, memos and newspapers use the clipped written style ('~음', '~함', noun endings); Lisa's diary uses short plain sentences; units are kept as in the source (inches, feet).
